NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a hybrid radial-axial bearing preload system with active thermal compensation using shape memory alloy (SMA) elements that dynamically adjusts bearing preload to compensate for thermal expansion during warmup cycles. Standard practice uses fixed mechanical preload that cannot adjust to thermal changes, leading to increased friction and heat generation. This is a departure from standard practice because it introduces a passive, self-adjusting mechanism that responds to temperature changes without external control systems or sensors. The closest existing technique is the use of hydraulic or pneumatic preload systems in some high-performance spindles, but those require external pumps, sensors, and control systems, whereas our SMA-based preload system is passive, self-contained, and operates purely on thermal response without external power or control.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the thermal expansion coefficient of the spindle shaft: ΔL = α·L·ΔT, where α for steel is ~12×10⁻⁶/°C. For a 200mm shaft section with 30°C temperature rise, this would cause 72μm of elongation. The SMA preload system counteracts this by increasing radial preload as temperature rises, reducing the bearing's internal clearance and maintaining consistent contact forces. The SMA elements (with transformation temperature ~45°C) will expand radially when heated, applying additional preload to compensate for thermal expansion. For a typical spindle bearing with 5μm initial clearance at 20°C, the SMA system can provide up to 8μm of additional preload at 50°C, reducing the effective thermal displacement to below 10μm.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components for installation:
- Standard bearing housing (no change)
- Standard precision bearings (no change)
- SMA preload elements (commercially available NiTi alloy wires, 0.5mm diameter) - REPLACE standard fixed shims
- SMA housing pockets (machined into existing bearing housing bore) - ADD to existing housing
- SMA activation channels (small holes in housing for heat transfer) - ADD to existing housing
- Temperature reference point (standard thermocouple port) - NO CHANGE (existing)

Procedure for installation:
1. Remove existing fixed bearing shims
2. Machine SMA pockets into bearing housing (within existing machining tolerances)
3. Insert pre-stressed SMA wires into pockets
4. Reassemble bearing assembly with standard procedures
5. No additional calibration required (self-adjusting)

Procedure for operation:
1. Standard startup procedure
2. System automatically adjusts during warmup without operator intervention
3. Standard machining operations resume when thermal equilibrium is reached

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Component/Process | Standard Practice | Proposed Intervention | Burden Impact |
|-------------------|-------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| Bearing housing | Standard housing | Housing with SMA pockets | Same (machining within existing tolerances) |
| Bearing shims | Fixed steel shims | SMA elements | Same (commercially available) |
| Assembly procedure | Standard assembly | Standard assembly with SMA insertion | Same |
| Control system | None | None | Same |
| Sensors | None | None | Same |
| Power requirements | None | None | Same |
| Maintenance | Standard bearing replacement | Standard bearing replacement | Same |
| Cost | Standard bearing cost | Standard bearing + SMA elements | Same (SMA elements are commodity items) |

Conclusion: Same burden class - The intervention uses commercially available SMA elements and machining within existing tolerances, requiring no additional infrastructure, control systems, or power supplies.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Mount test spindle in temperature-controlled chamber
2. Install calibrated displacement sensors at bearing locations and tool holder
3. Mount test artifact with known geometry
4. Run warmup cycle from 20°C to 50°C at standard startup rate
5. Record displacement measurements at 1-minute intervals
6. After thermal equilibrium, perform test cuts and measure part dimensions

Instruments:
- 3-axis displacement laser measurement system (±0.5μm accuracy)
- Type K thermocouples (±0.1°C accuracy)
- Temperature chamber (±0.5°C control)
- Precision test artifact
- CMM for part measurement (±1μm accuracy)

Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- Maximum tool center point displacement during warmup must remain below 10μm
- Post-warmup part tolerance must be within 2μm of cold operation tolerance
- Test duration: 20 minutes warmup + 5 minutes machining

Kill Criterion:
- If displacement exceeds 10μm at any point during warmup
- If post-warmup part tolerance exceeds 150% of cold operation tolerance
- If SMA system shows signs of fatigue after 5 thermal cycles
